items.title: Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1957-04-20
items.q: Louis wrote to me and told me he was going to leave Fletcher. He heard I was coming to Chicago, what I record with him, you know. Then I worked at Dreamland with Louis after that, you see.

ctx.x: What was the first record session in Chicago?

Hot Five. Hot Five. Hot Five. Louis wrote to me and told me he was going to leave Fletcher. He heard I was coming to Chicago, what I record with him, you know. Then I worked at Dreamland with Louis after that, you see. After the... Dutry got well and I was waiting for him.
I asked Ed one question. Why he didn't have a band of his own in Chicago. Yeah. You know the answer I got? He was fed up with the responsibilities. Yeah.

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: I hired Louis before Joe left.

ctx.x: That wasn't the place on the array. It was on the labor?
The labor ran between Conti and St. Louis. About near St. Louis. I hired Louis before Joe left.
That's what I'm saying. I come back, I find Louis.

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: All of them. Kid Ory, Bunk Johnson.

ctx.x: Louis, who would you say was the greatest influence on your life? Not in your youth, not musicians, I mean individuals. In your family or?

Well, my mother, she taught us the real things. She always said, you probably never get rich. She was wrong there, wasn't she? Well, she might be. Maybe, you know, maybe $10 million to save $10, you know. But I mean, what she means were have yachts and still got a zillion. We wasn't even thinking about that. She wasn't even thinking about it when she told me, say, but you'll always have health. So take a laxative every night of your life. And that's the finest things you ever told me. You didn't have much money…
When did you leave New Orleans?
